mainTopic: The ברייתא about buying wine from כותים on ערב שבת, and רבי מאיר's ruling that one may designate future tithes now and drink right away. This relies on the principle of ברירה (retroactive clarification).
overview: This amud finishes a ברייתא that the גמרא quotes in its discussion of ברירה. A person bought wine from כותים, who cannot be trusted to have tithed it, and has no time to separate the gifts before שבת. He declares in words that portions he will separate later are already the gifts. Ten לוג will be מעשר ראשון and nine לוג will be מעשר שני. He redeems the מעשר שני on coins and may drink right away. This is רבי מאיר's ruling. It works because he holds יש ברירה: the later separation shows retroactively which wine was the gifts all along.

steps.title: רבי מאיר allows designating future tithes now and drinking immediately
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes listing what the buyer declares: ten לוג are מעשר ראשון and nine לוג are מעשר שני. He redeems the מעשר שני and may drink right away. This is רבי מאיר's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Ten [לוג that I will separate later] are מעשר ראשון, nine are מעשר שני. Then he redeems [the מעשר שני on money] and drinks immediately." These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting the rest of a ברייתא as a source in its discussion of ברירה. The buyer names, in words only, which future portions of the wine will be מעשר ראשון and מעשר שני. רבי מאיר then rules that he may drink right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing is physically separated yet. The buyer only says that the portions he will remove later are the gifts. רבי מאיר lets him drink now because he holds יש ברירה: once the gifts are actually separated after שבת, it becomes clear retroactively that the wine he drank was never the gifts. The גמרא cites this ruling because it shows who accepts ברירה. The other תנאים, who forbid drinking, do not accept it.

keyTerms.meaning: First tithe: one tenth of the produce, given to the לוי
Second tithe: a tenth of what remains, eaten in ירושלים or redeemed with money
Redeems (= מְחַלֵּל): transfers the holiness of מעשר שני onto coins
Immediately: right now, without waiting until after שבת
Retroactive clarification: a later choice reveals what was true from the beginning
A liquid measure; the case assumes 100 לוג of wine

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר holds יש ברירה. A person may designate gifts in words now, separate them physically later, and drink immediately, because the later separation clarifies everything retroactively.
steps.confusionAlert: Why is מעשר שני only nine לוג and not ten? From 100 לוג, two go to תרומה (counted in the earlier part of the ברייתא). Ten go to מעשר ראשון, which is a tenth of the 98 remaining, rounded. That leaves about 88–90. מעשר שני is a tenth of that remainder, so it is nine and not ten.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is a well-known source showing which תנאים hold of ברירה. Here רבי מאיר permits, while רבי יהודה, רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון forbid. That is why the גמרא brings it into the סוגיא to clarify a תנא's position on ברירה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a ברייתא whose opening (the purchase from כותים and the two לוג of תרומה) appeared on the previous amud.
steps.raayaObject: Which תנאים accept the principle of ברירה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of הלוקח יין מבין הכותים: רבי מאיר permits immediate drinking based on future separation
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, one may verbally designate future portions as מעשר ראשון and מעשר שני, redeem the מעשר שני, and drink immediately, because יש ברירה.
